To time a magneto to the engine, the following steps are taken:

1.  **Prepare the Magneto Internally:** Before installation, the internal timing of the magneto must be checked and adjusted with the magneto off the engine. This involves positioning the magneto rotor at the E-gap position and setting the breaker points to open when the timing lines or marks are perfectly aligned [1].
2.  **Position the Engine:** Remove the most accessible spark plug from the No. 1 cylinder. Pull the propeller through in the direction of rotation until the No. 1 piston is coming up on the compression stroke, which can be felt by holding a thumb over the spark plug hole [2].
3.  **Set Crankshaft Position:** Set the engine crankshaft at the prescribed number of degrees ahead of true top dead center on the compression stroke, usually using the timing marks on the engine [2].
4.  **Install the Magneto:** While holding the magneto drive in the firing position for the No. 1 cylinder as indicated by the alignment of the reference marks, install the magneto drive into the engine drive [2]. The magneto should be installed in the middle of its slotted flange to allow for fine timing [2].
5.  **Check Point Opening:** Attach a timing light to both magnetos. With the engine still in the firing position, move the magnetos in the flange slots until the breaker points in the magneto just open [2]. If the slots do not permit sufficient movement, move the magneto out of position to permit turning the magneto drive shaft, then reinstall and repeat the check [2].
6.  **Verify Synchronization:** Ensure that the lights for both sets of points come on when the points are open, within the prescribed timing position [3]. Both right and left sets of breaker points should open at the same instant to ensure proper magneto-to-engine timing and synchronized operation [3].

The four conditions that must occur at the same instant for correct timing are: the piston in the No. 1 cylinder is a prescribed number of degrees before top dead center on the compression stroke; the rotating magnet of the magneto is in the E-gap position; the breaker points are just opening on the No. 1 cam lobe; and the distributor finger is aligned with the electrode serving the No. 1 cylinder [4].
